study_identification.title: Sex differences in normative modeling of cortical thickness in cannabis use disorder

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: GLMs tested associations between cortical thickness z-scores (regions with sex differences) and behavioral measures (MCQ craving, MJPS cannabis-associated problems, BIS impulsivity) with sex interaction; 3 regions (pars orbitalis, superior parietal cortex, precuneus) positively associated with MJPS; postcentral gyrus negatively associated with MCQ.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Both sexes showed normative-average cortical thickness overall; females exhibited higher cortical thickness z-scores than males in several regions; three sexually dimorphic regions’ z-scores related to cannabis-related problems.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Average z-scores across regions were within normative ranges for both sexes. Total cortical thickness z-scores were greater in females; 14 regions (around central and lateral sulci) had greater z-scores in females; medial orbitofrontal cortex z-score was greater in males. Of these, pars orbitalis, superior parietal cortex, and precuneus z-scores positively correlated with MJPS; postcentral gyrus z-score negatively correlated with MCQ.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Modest sample size, particularly females; retrospective self-report of use; restrictive inclusion/exclusion may limit generalizability; secondary analysis of baseline RCT data without control of hormonal/physiological factors (e.g., contraceptive use, menstrual phase, time of day); tobacco use not fully controlled historically; cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; sex assessed by self-report only.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Findings suggest sex-related cortical thickness differences in CUD with limited immediate clinical application; potential utility for stratifying subgroups with deviations and relating to outcomes merits future longitudinal work.

general_notes.general_notes: MRI single-site Siemens 3T Prisma; FreeSurfer v6.0 segmentation; NOMIS Python script used for z-scores. NOMIS reference sample characteristics (beyond n and age range) are not detailed here; see Potvin et al. 2016/2017/2022. Supplementary tables report hemisphere correlations and sex differences for hippocampal/cerebellar z-scores.
